chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Moses (peace be upon him) supplicated, and Aaron (peace be upon him) said 'Ameen', and the Angels (peace be upon them) said 'Ameen'. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'Your supplication has been accepted, therefore be steadfast.'
And whoever fights in the Way of Allah, he will be answered, just as He answered for both of you, on the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Moses' supplication regarding the acceptance of du'a for those who strive in God's path?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the prophetic tradition of 'tasmīn' (affirmation) by Aaron and the angels, establishing a divine precedent for the efficacy of collective supplication. It extends this spiritual principle to the concept of jihad, promising that those who strive in God's path will have their prayers answered on the Day of Judgment with the same certainty granted to Moses and Aaron, thereby linking physical struggle with spiritual acceptance.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Musaas supplicated and Harounas said ‘Ameen’, and the Angels (also) said, ‘Ameen’.

So Allahazwj Blessed and High Said [10:89] He said: I have Accepted the supplication of both of you, therefore be steadfast; and (for) the one who fights in the Way of Allahazwj, Iazwj shall Answer for him just as Iazwj Answered for both of youas, up to the Day of Judgment”’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Moses prayed and Hamn said Amin and the angels said Amin. Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, then said, “I have accepted your prayer be steadfast”, [10:89]
and the prayer of one who fights for the cause of Allah will be answered just like the prayer of two of you (Moses and Hamn) is accepted to the Day of Judgment.’”
